en.title: English proverbs & idioms — 25 natives
en.blurb: Well-worn English sayings that still show up in conversation — with what they actually mean when used.

items.text: A stitch in time saves nine.
items.translation: A stitch in time saves nine.

meta.meaning: Act on a problem early — a small fix now prevents a big one later.

items.text: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.
items.translation: Don't count your chickens before they hatch.

meta.meaning: Don't assume success before it's actually confirmed.

items.text: The early bird catches the worm.
items.translation: The early bird catches the worm.

meta.meaning: People who start early get the best opportunities.

items.translation: Actions speak louder than words.

meta.meaning: What you do matters more than what you say.

items.text: Every cloud has a silver lining.
items.translation: Every cloud has a silver lining.

meta.meaning: Even bad situations have something positive hidden in them.

items.text: The grass is always greener on the other side.
items.translation: The grass is always greener on the other side.

meta.meaning: People tend to envy others' situations rather than appreciating their own.

items.text: You can't judge a book by its cover.
items.translation: You can't judge a book by its cover.

meta.meaning: Appearances can be misleading — don't decide too quickly.

items.text: Rome wasn't built in a day.
items.translation: Rome wasn't built in a day.

meta.meaning: Big things take time — be patient.

items.text: When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
items.translation: When in Rome, do as the Romans do.

meta.meaning: When you're somewhere new, follow the local customs.

items.translation: A watched pot never boils.

meta.meaning: Waiting anxiously for something makes it feel slower.

items.translation: Barking up the wrong tree.

meta.meaning: To look for a solution in the wrong place or blame the wrong person.

items.text: Hit the nail on the head.
items.translation: Hit the nail on the head.

meta.meaning: To describe something exactly right.

items.translation: Spill the beans.

meta.meaning: To reveal a secret, usually accidentally.

items.translation: Bite the bullet.

meta.meaning: To force yourself to do something unpleasant you've been avoiding.

items.translation: Break the ice.

meta.meaning: To make people feel more comfortable at the start of a social situation.

items.translation: Call it a day.

meta.meaning: To stop working on something, usually for the rest of the day.

items.text: Cost an arm and a leg.
items.translation: Cost an arm and a leg.

meta.meaning: To be very expensive.

items.translation: Beat around the bush.

meta.meaning: To avoid saying something directly.

items.translation: Burn the midnight oil.

meta.meaning: To work very late into the night.

items.text: The ball is in your court.
items.translation: The ball is in your court.

meta.meaning: It's now your turn to act or decide.

items.text: You can't have your cake and eat it too.
items.translation: You can't have your cake and eat it too.

meta.meaning: You can't enjoy two incompatible benefits at the same time.

items.translation: Better late than never.

meta.meaning: It's better to do something late than to never do it at all.

items.translation: Practice makes perfect.

meta.meaning: Repeated practice leads to mastery.

items.text: Where there's a will, there's a way.
items.translation: Where there's a will, there's a way.

meta.meaning: If you're determined enough, you'll find a way to succeed.

items.text: Birds of a feather flock together.
items.translation: Birds of a feather flock together.

meta.meaning: People with similar interests tend to spend time together.

es.title: Refranes españoles — 25 frases vivas
es.blurb: Refranes y modismos que todavía se oyen en la calle — con lo que de verdad significan al usarlos.

items.text: A caballo regalado no le mires el diente.
items.translation: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

meta.meaning: No critiques algo que te han regalado.

items.text: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.
items.translation: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

meta.meaning: Es mejor lo seguro que no lo mucho pero incierto.

items.text: No por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano.
items.translation: You can't rush time by rising earlier.

meta.meaning: Las cosas tienen su ritmo; apurarse no las acelera.

items.text: En boca cerrada no entran moscas.
items.translation: Flies don't fly into a closed mouth.

meta.meaning: A veces vale más callar.

items.translation: Put on a brave face when things go wrong.

meta.meaning: Ante lo que va mal, actitud positiva.

items.text: Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres.
items.translation: Tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are.

meta.meaning: Las compañías dicen mucho de alguien.

items.text: No es oro todo lo que reluce.
items.translation: Not all that glitters is gold.

meta.meaning: Lo que brilla por fuera no siempre vale por dentro.

items.translation: Better late than never.

meta.meaning: Mejor hacerlo con retraso que no hacerlo.

items.text: A quien madruga, Dios le ayuda.
items.translation: God helps those who rise early.

meta.meaning: Al que se esfuerza y se adelanta le va mejor.

items.text: Camarón que se duerme, se lo lleva la corriente.
items.translation: A sleeping shrimp gets swept away by the current.

meta.meaning: Si te descuidas, pierdes la oportunidad.

items.text: No hay mal que por bien no venga.
items.translation: There's no evil that doesn't bring some good.

meta.meaning: Las desgracias pueden traer algo bueno al final.

items.translation: Cobbler, stick to your shoes.

meta.meaning: Cada uno a lo suyo, no te metas donde no sabes.

items.text: El que no llora, no mama.
items.translation: The one who doesn't cry doesn't get fed.

meta.meaning: Si no pides, no consigues.

items.text: Más sabe el diablo por viejo que por diablo.
items.translation: The devil knows more from being old than from being the devil.

meta.meaning: La experiencia enseña más que la astucia.

items.text: No dejes para mañana lo que puedas hacer hoy.
items.translation: Don't leave for tomorrow what you can do today.

meta.meaning: No postergues lo que ya puedes resolver.

items.text: El que mucho abarca, poco aprieta.
items.translation: He who grasps too much holds little tightly.

meta.meaning: Abarcar demasiado hace que no termines nada bien.

items.text: Ojos que no ven, corazón que no siente.
items.translation: Eyes that don't see, heart that doesn't feel.

meta.meaning: Lo que no conocemos no nos duele.

items.translation: Great ills demand great remedies.

meta.meaning: Los problemas serios piden soluciones serias.

items.translation: A barking dog seldom bites.

meta.meaning: El que mucho amenaza suele hacer poco.

items.text: Hablando del rey de Roma, por la puerta asoma.
items.translation: Speak of the king of Rome, and he appears at the door.

meta.meaning: Equivalente a 'speak of the devil'.

items.text: A falta de pan, buenas son tortas.
items.translation: If there's no bread, cakes will do.

meta.meaning: A veces nos conformamos con lo que hay.

items.translation: Time heals everything.

meta.meaning: Con el paso del tiempo, las heridas duelen menos.

items.text: Al pan, pan y al vino, vino.
items.translation: Call bread 'bread' and wine 'wine'.

meta.meaning: Hablar claro, llamar a las cosas por su nombre.

items.translation: Cheap things end up expensive.

meta.meaning: Comprar lo barato muchas veces sale más caro al final.

items.text: Nunca es tarde si la dicha es buena.
items.translation: It's never too late if the outcome is good.

meta.meaning: Si algo bueno llega, el momento siempre es apropiado.

fr.title: Proverbes français — 25 expressions bien vivantes
fr.blurb: Les proverbes et expressions qu'on entend encore — avec ce qu'ils veulent vraiment dire.

items.text: Qui ne tente rien n'a rien.
items.translation: He who tries nothing has nothing.

meta.meaning: Il faut oser pour obtenir quelque chose.

items.text: L'habit ne fait pas le moine.
items.translation: The habit doesn't make the monk.

meta.meaning: L'apparence ne révèle pas qui l'on est vraiment.

items.text: Petit à petit, l'oiseau fait son nid.
items.translation: Little by little, the bird builds its nest.

meta.meaning: Les grandes choses se construisent par petits efforts.

items.text: Qui vole un œuf vole un bœuf.
items.translation: He who steals an egg will steal an ox.

meta.meaning: Une petite malhonnêteté peut mener à de plus grandes.

items.translation: Better late than never.

meta.meaning: Mieux faire quelque chose en retard que pas du tout.

items.text: Il ne faut pas vendre la peau de l'ours avant de l'avoir tué.
items.translation: Don't sell the bear's skin before killing it.

meta.meaning: Ne pas se réjouir d'un résultat avant qu'il soit sûr.

items.text: C'est en forgeant qu'on devient forgeron.
items.translation: It's by forging that one becomes a blacksmith.

meta.meaning: On apprend un métier en le pratiquant.

items.translation: Appetite comes while eating.

meta.meaning: Plus on commence une chose, plus on en veut.

items.text: Après la pluie, le beau temps.
items.translation: After the rain, fine weather.

meta.meaning: Les moments difficiles finissent toujours par passer.

items.text: Un tiens vaut mieux que deux tu l'auras.
items.translation: One 'take it' is worth more than two 'you'll have it'.

meta.meaning: Il vaut mieux ce qu'on a que ce qu'on espère.

items.text: Il n'y a pas de fumée sans feu.
items.translation: There's no smoke without fire.

meta.meaning: Toute rumeur a souvent un fond de vérité.

items.translation: A scalded cat fears cold water.

meta.meaning: Après une mauvaise expérience, on devient très prudent.

items.translation: He who sleeps dines.

meta.meaning: Dormir fait oublier la faim ; profiter de ce qu'on a.

items.text: On ne fait pas d'omelette sans casser des œufs.
items.translation: You can't make an omelette without breaking eggs.

meta.meaning: Pour obtenir un résultat, il faut accepter quelques sacrifices.

items.translation: The walls have ears.

meta.meaning: Attention à ce qu'on dit, on peut toujours être entendu.

items.text: Qui va à la chasse perd sa place.
items.translation: He who goes hunting loses his place.

meta.meaning: Si on quitte sa place, on peut la perdre.

items.translation: Prevention is better than cure.

meta.meaning: Agir avant qu'un problème n'apparaisse est plus efficace.

items.translation: Union makes strength.

meta.meaning: Ensemble, on est plus fort que seuls.

items.text: Rien ne sert de courir, il faut partir à point.
items.translation: There's no use running — you must leave in time.

meta.meaning: Mieux vaut bien préparer que se précipiter.

items.text: Qui sème le vent récolte la tempête.
items.translation: He who sows the wind reaps the storm.

meta.meaning: Les mauvaises actions reviennent, amplifiées.

items.translation: To err is human.

meta.meaning: Tout le monde fait des erreurs — c'est normal.

items.translation: He who lives will see.

meta.meaning: Seul le temps dira ce qui va se passer.

items.translation: To a brave heart, nothing is impossible.

meta.meaning: Avec du courage, on peut tout accomplir.

items.text: Les cordonniers sont les plus mal chaussés.
items.translation: Cobblers are the worst shod.

meta.meaning: Les experts négligent souvent ce qu'ils savent faire pour eux-mêmes.

items.text: On n'est jamais mieux servi que par soi-même.
items.translation: You're never better served than by yourself.

meta.meaning: Si tu veux que ce soit bien fait, fais-le toi-même.

de.title: Deutsche Sprichwörter & Redewendungen — 25 lebendige
de.blurb: Sprichwörter und Redewendungen, die man im Alltag noch hört — mit ihrer eigentlichen Bedeutung.

items.translation: The morning hour has gold in its mouth.

meta.meaning: Wer früh aufsteht, schafft mehr.

items.translation: Practice makes the master.

meta.meaning: Durch Üben wird man gut in einer Sache.

items.text: Wer anderen eine Grube gräbt, fällt selbst hinein.
items.translation: He who digs a pit for others falls into it himself.

meta.meaning: Böse Absichten schlagen auf einen selbst zurück.

items.translation: All beginnings are difficult.

meta.meaning: Am Anfang ist jede Sache mühsam.

items.translation: Lies have short legs.

meta.meaning: Lügen kommen schnell ans Licht.

items.text: Was Hänschen nicht lernt, lernt Hans nimmermehr.
items.translation: What little Hans doesn't learn, big Hans will never learn.

meta.meaning: Was man als Kind lernt, prägt einen das Leben lang.

items.translation: Small cattle also make manure.

meta.meaning: Auch kleine Beiträge summieren sich.

items.translation: No diligence, no prize.

meta.meaning: Ohne Anstrengung gibt es keinen Erfolg.

items.translation: He who rests, rusts.

meta.meaning: Wer nichts tut, verliert mit der Zeit seine Fähigkeiten.

items.translation: Dogs that bark don't bite.

meta.meaning: Wer viel droht, tut meistens wenig.

items.text: Reden ist Silber, Schweigen ist Gold.
items.translation: Speech is silver, silence is gold.

meta.meaning: Manchmal ist es klüger zu schweigen.

items.text: Der Apfel fällt nicht weit vom Stamm.
items.translation: The apple doesn't fall far from the trunk.

meta.meaning: Kinder ähneln oft ihren Eltern.

items.text: Wo ein Wille ist, ist auch ein Weg.
items.translation: Where there's a will, there's a way.

meta.meaning: Mit genug Entschlossenheit findet sich ein Weg.

items.text: Zwei Fliegen mit einer Klappe schlagen.
items.translation: To hit two flies with one swat.

meta.meaning: Mit einer Handlung zwei Ziele erreichen.

items.translation: That's where the dog is buried.

meta.meaning: Da liegt der eigentliche Kern des Problems.

items.translation: To tie a bear onto someone.

meta.meaning: Jemandem eine erfundene Geschichte aufzwingen.

items.text: Alles hat ein Ende, nur die Wurst hat zwei.
items.translation: Everything has an end, only the sausage has two.

meta.meaning: Humorvoller Hinweis, dass alles einmal zu Ende geht.

items.translation: To speak through flowers.

meta.meaning: Etwas indirekt oder beschönigend sagen.

items.text: Den Nagel auf den Kopf treffen.
items.translation: To hit the nail on the head.

meta.meaning: Genau das Richtige sagen oder treffen.

items.text: Nicht alle Tassen im Schrank haben.
items.translation: To not have all cups in the cupboard.

meta.meaning: Umgangssprachlich: nicht ganz bei Verstand sein.

items.translation: To step on someone's tie.

meta.meaning: Jemanden unabsichtlich kränken.

items.text: Da wird der Hund in der Pfanne verrückt.
items.translation: That makes the dog crazy in the pan.

meta.meaning: Ausdruck großer Überraschung oder Fassungslosigkeit.

items.translation: Too many cooks spoil the porridge.

meta.meaning: Zu viele Beteiligte machen eine Sache schlechter.

items.text: Was lange währt, wird endlich gut.
items.translation: What takes a long time finally becomes good.

meta.meaning: Qualität braucht Zeit.

items.text: In der Kürze liegt die Würze.
items.translation: In brevity lies the spice.

meta.meaning: Kurz und knackig ist am wirkungsvollsten.

it.title: Proverbi e modi di dire italiani — 25 vivi
it.blurb: Proverbi e modi di dire che si sentono ancora oggi — con ciò che significano davvero.

items.translation: He who sleeps catches no fish.

meta.meaning: Chi è pigro non ottiene risultati.

items.translation: Better late than never.

meta.meaning: Meglio arrivare in ritardo che non arrivare affatto.

items.text: Fra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare.
items.translation: Between saying and doing there's the sea.

meta.meaning: Dire una cosa è facile, farla è molto più difficile.

items.text: Chi va piano va sano e va lontano.
items.translation: He who goes slowly goes safely and far.

meta.meaning: Chi non ha fretta ottiene risultati migliori.

items.text: Non è tutto oro quel che luccica.
items.translation: Not all that glitters is gold.

meta.meaning: Le apparenze possono ingannare.

items.text: L'ospite è come il pesce, dopo tre giorni puzza.
items.translation: A guest is like a fish — after three days he stinks.

meta.meaning: Un ospite non dovrebbe restare troppo a lungo.

items.text: Il mattino ha l'oro in bocca.
items.translation: The morning has gold in its mouth.

meta.meaning: Alzandoti presto si fa molto di più.

items.translation: He who does it, should expect it back.

meta.meaning: Chi fa del male deve aspettarsi che gli torni indietro.

items.text: A caval donato non si guarda in bocca.
items.translation: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.

meta.meaning: Non si critica un regalo.

items.text: Rosso di sera, bel tempo si spera.
items.translation: Red sky at night, fine weather hoped for.

meta.meaning: Il cielo rosso di sera di solito promette bel tempo.

items.text: Chi trova un amico, trova un tesoro.
items.translation: He who finds a friend finds a treasure.

meta.meaning: Un vero amico vale moltissimo.

items.text: L'erba del vicino è sempre più verde.
items.translation: The neighbour's grass is always greener.

meta.meaning: Spesso si pensa che gli altri abbiano meglio di noi.

items.translation: He who stays silent consents.

meta.meaning: Non dire nulla equivale a essere d'accordo.

items.translation: To make merchant's ears.

meta.meaning: Fingere di non sentire ciò che non si vuole sentire.

items.translation: In the mouth of the wolf!

meta.meaning: Modo di dire 'buona fortuna' — si risponde 'crepi il lupo'.

items.translation: To have one's hands in the dough.

meta.meaning: Essere coinvolti in qualcosa, spesso con interessi personali.

items.translation: Not to see the hour.

meta.meaning: Essere impazienti di qualcosa.

items.text: Fare il passo più lungo della gamba.
items.translation: To take a step longer than one's leg.

meta.meaning: Fare qualcosa di eccessivo per le proprie capacità.

items.text: Tutte le strade portano a Roma.
items.translation: All roads lead to Rome.

meta.meaning: Ci sono molti modi per arrivare allo stesso risultato.

items.translation: He who sows wind reaps storm.

meta.meaning: Le cattive azioni portano guai ancora più grandi.

items.translation: To a wise listener, few words suffice.

meta.meaning: Chi capisce al volo non ha bisogno di spiegazioni lunghe.

items.translation: There's no two without three.

meta.meaning: Dopo due eventi simili ne arriva spesso un terzo.

items.translation: He who endures wins.

meta.meaning: La costanza porta al successo.

items.text: Prendere due piccioni con una fava.
items.translation: To get two pigeons with one broad bean.

meta.meaning: Ottenere due risultati con una sola azione.

items.text: Chi va con lo zoppo impara a zoppicare.
items.translation: He who walks with a limper learns to limp.

meta.meaning: Le cattive compagnie influenzano.

pt.title: Provérbios em português — 25 ditados vivos
pt.blurb: Ditados e expressões que ainda aparecem na conversa — com o que de fato significam quando usados.

items.translation: Who doesn't risk, doesn't snack.

meta.meaning: Sem correr algum risco, não dá para conseguir nada.

items.text: Mais vale um pássaro na mão do que dois voando.
items.translation: A bird in the hand is worth two flying.

meta.meaning: O que está garantido vale mais que a promessa de mais.

items.text: Água mole em pedra dura, tanto bate até que fura.
items.translation: Soft water on hard stone — keeps hitting till it bores through.

meta.meaning: Com persistência, até o mais difícil cede.

items.text: A pressa é inimiga da perfeição.
items.translation: Haste is the enemy of perfection.

meta.meaning: Querer rápido demais prejudica a qualidade.

items.text: Em casa de ferreiro, espeto de pau.
items.translation: In the blacksmith's house, a wooden skewer.

meta.meaning: Especialistas às vezes não aplicam a si o que ensinam.

items.translation: He who wants everything loses everything.

meta.meaning: A ganância costuma trazer prejuízo.

items.translation: The cheap turns out expensive.

meta.meaning: Comprar barato muitas vezes custa mais no fim.

items.translation: Going slowly, one goes far.

meta.meaning: A pressa não é melhor caminho; a constância vale mais.

items.translation: Better late than never.

meta.meaning: Fazer algo com atraso é melhor que não fazer.

items.text: Diga-me com quem andas, e te direi quem és.
items.translation: Tell me who you walk with, and I'll tell you who you are.

meta.meaning: As companhias dizem muito sobre a pessoa.

items.translation: A dog that barks doesn't bite.

meta.meaning: Quem muito ameaça costuma fazer pouco.

items.text: Macaco velho não põe a mão em cumbuca.
items.translation: An old monkey doesn't put its hand in a trap jar.

meta.meaning: Quem tem experiência não cai nos mesmos erros.

items.text: Quando a esmola é demais, o santo desconfia.
items.translation: When the alms are too much, the saint grows suspicious.

meta.meaning: Bondade exagerada esconde segundas intenções.

items.text: Casa de ferreiro, espeto de pau.
items.translation: Blacksmith's house, wooden skewer.

meta.meaning: Variante — profissionais nem sempre aplicam o próprio ofício.

items.translation: Union makes strength.

meta.meaning: Juntos somos mais fortes do que separados.

items.text: Nem tudo que reluz é ouro.
items.translation: Not all that shines is gold.

meta.meaning: O que parece bonito nem sempre vale muito.

items.text: A vingança é um prato que se come frio.
items.translation: Revenge is a dish best served cold.

meta.meaning: A vingança é melhor planejada com calma.

items.text: Quem conta um conto aumenta um ponto.
items.translation: He who tells a tale adds a point.

meta.meaning: As histórias crescem a cada vez que são contadas.

items.text: Depois da tempestade, vem a bonança.
items.translation: After the storm comes calm.

meta.meaning: Momentos difíceis sempre passam.

items.text: Pau que nasce torto, morre torto.
items.translation: A stick born crooked dies crooked.

meta.meaning: O que começa torto raramente se endireita.

items.text: Para bom entendedor, meia palavra basta.
items.translation: For a good listener, half a word is enough.

meta.meaning: Quem é esperto entende sem precisar de muita explicação.

items.text: Em terra de cego, quem tem um olho é rei.
items.translation: In the land of the blind, the one-eyed man is king.

meta.meaning: Entre os ignorantes, até um pequeno conhecimento já basta.

items.translation: God helps those who rise early.

meta.meaning: Quem acorda cedo e trabalha costuma colher bons resultados.

items.translation: He who sows wind reaps storm.

meta.meaning: As más ações voltam ampliadas.

items.translation: Better to prevent than to cure.

meta.meaning: Evitar um problema é mais barato que resolvê-lo depois.

ja.title: 日本のことわざ — 25 の生きた表現
ja.blurb: 今も日常会話に出てくる日本のことわざと慣用句 — 本当の意味とともに。

items.translation: Even monkeys fall from trees.

meta.meaning: どんな達人でも失敗することがある。

items.translation: Three years on a stone.

meta.meaning: 辛抱すれば必ず結果が出る。

items.translation: Fall seven times, rise eight.

meta.meaning: 何度失敗しても諦めずに立ち上がる。

items.translation: Dumplings over flowers.

meta.meaning: 見た目より実利を取ること。

items.translation: The nail that sticks out gets hammered down.

meta.meaning: 目立つ人は批判や嫉妬を受けやすい。

items.text: 井の中の蛙大海を知らず。
items.translation: A frog in a well doesn't know the ocean.

meta.meaning: 狭い世界しか知らないと広い世界が見えない。

items.text: 塵も積もれば山となる。
items.translation: Even dust piles up to form a mountain.

meta.meaning: 小さなことも積み重ねれば大きくなる。

items.translation: Fortune comes to the smiling gate.

meta.meaning: いつも笑って過ごす家には幸運が訪れる。

items.text: 虎穴に入らずんば虎子を得ず。
items.translation: If you don't enter the tiger's cave, you can't catch the tiger's cub.

meta.meaning: リスクを取らなければ大きな成果は得られない。

items.translation: When hurried, take the long way.

meta.meaning: 急いでいる時こそ安全で確実な道を選ぶ。

items.translation: A skilled hawk hides its talons.

meta.meaning: 本当に力のある人は、自分の力を見せびらかさない。

items.text: 二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず。
items.translation: He who chases two rabbits catches neither.

meta.meaning: 欲張ると結局両方失う。

items.text: 郷に入っては郷に従え。
items.translation: When you enter a village, follow its customs.

meta.meaning: 新しい場所ではその土地のやり方に合わせる。

items.translation: The mouth is the source of misfortune.

meta.meaning: 軽はずみな発言がトラブルを招く。

items.translation: Seeing once is better than hearing a hundred times.

meta.meaning: 何度も聞くより一度見るほうが分かる。

items.text: 親しき仲にも礼儀あり。
items.translation: Even between close friends, courtesy is needed.

meta.meaning: 親しくても礼儀を忘れないこと。

items.translation: Even bugs eat knotweed — tastes differ.

meta.meaning: 好みは人それぞれ。

items.translation: A metal club to an ogre.

meta.meaning: もともと強いものがさらに強くなる。

items.translation: Even Kobo makes mistakes with a brush.

meta.meaning: 名人でもミスをする。

items.translation: If you're prepared, you have no worries.

meta.meaning: 事前に準備しておけば困らない。
